newsitem.title: JAPAN: Malaysia's Mahathir calls for Japanese investment.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Mahathir calls for Japanese investment.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad called on Wednesday for further Japanese investment, particularly in his country's proposed multi-media zone.

"I am hopeful that Japan will...increase its participation in line with the changing pattern in Malaysia where the emphasis is now on investment in high technology and capital intensive sector," Mahathir said.

"The Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC) project that we have just launched is one area where we would like to invite Japanese participation," Mahathir said in a speech before a banquet hosted by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.

Hashimoto told Mahathir he was aware of the Malaysian Prime Minister's strong interest in Japanese technology in relation to the MSC project and called for the two countries to strengthen their partnership and to discuss a wider range of issues.

"With both countries' roles and responsibilities in the international community having expanded, our relationship has grown closer and as a result our two countries are now required to discuss a wider spectrum of issues," Hashimoto said in his welcoming speech.
Mahathir is in Japan on an official visit to Japan from Tuesday through to Saturday. He will visit the western city of Osaka from Thursday.
